staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer crash against this preserved vulnerable checkout. Stage 02 uses the exact staged source, patch, sanitizer trace, default crash trace, reproduction report, and testcase bytes, and keeps the closed trace limited to states directly established by those artifacts.

classification.classification_note: The saved sanitizer trace shows a size-1 global-buffer-overflow READ in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` at `HTMLparser.c:2759`. The out-of-bounds access happens when the parser re-evaluates the `CUR` macro in the attribute-scanning loop header while processing the attacker-supplied HTML document.

bug_description.original: A global-buffer-overflow exists in htmlParseHTMLAttribute (HTMLparser.c): the parser performs an out‑of‑bounds read (one byte) past a global string/array into adjacent global data (e.g. xmlIsPubidChar_tab) while parsing attribute text. This out‑of‑bounds access can cause crashes, undefined behavior, or potential information disclosure when processing crafted HTML attributes.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the exact saved witness with the OSS-Fuzz HTML target and observed `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` at `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` line 2759. In the harness, the first 8 testcase bytes are consumed as `opts` and `maxAlloc`, and the remaining 248 bytes are materialized as an HTML document. The staged testcase bytes show that this document begins with `<meta charset=TSCII>`, so the parser admits the input as HTML, parses the opening meta tag, extracts attacker-controlled attribute values, and switches decoding to TSCII through project code before later continuing to parse another attribute value. On the reproduced path, `htmlParseAttValue()` calls `htmlParseHTMLAttribute(ctxt, 0)`, and the saved sanitizer report proves that the subsequent loop-header evaluation of `CUR` in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` performs the crashing one-byte read just past a global one-byte string object. The staged patch discusses a memory-error propagation obligation in converted-input growth, but the saved runtime artifacts here do not prove that intermediate OOM sequence on the crashing run, so the closed GT keeps the witnessed contract at the parser, charset-switch, and sink states directly established by the source and traces.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled document bytes on the reproduced pull-parser path by materializing them into a parser context.
source.value_from: In `fuzz/html.c`, `docBuffer = xmlFuzzReadRemaining(&docSize);` passes the remaining testcase bytes to `htmlReadMemory()`. For this exact witness, the first 8 bytes are harness metadata and the remaining 248 bytes begin with `<meta charset=TSCII>`.

sink.description: Crash sink from the saved AddressSanitizer report. Re-evaluating `CUR` in this loop header performs the witnessed one-byte out-of-bounds read.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable loop re-reads the parser cursor through `CUR` without a source-grounded proof, on this crashing path, that the cursor still points inside a valid converted input buffer. The saved trace proves this dereference reads one byte past a global one-byte string object.

tainted_value_origin.description: The HTML bytes that later form the `<meta charset=TSCII>` tag and the attribute text parsed at the sink originate from this attacker-controlled document materialization point.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser gate. The staged testcase document begins with `<meta`, so this branch accepts the witness as an HTML start tag and routes execution into element parsing.

coarse_trace.summary: The pull parser materializes the attacker-controlled HTML document and admits it as an HTML start tag because the document begins with `<meta`.
Start-tag parsing extracts the attacker-controlled `charset=TSCII` meta attribute and switches the parser to TSCII decoding.
Later attribute parsing reaches `htmlParseHTMLAttribute(ctxt, 0)` on the same attacker-controlled document.
The saved ASan run crashes when the loop header at line 2759 re-evaluates `CUR` and reads one byte out of bounds.

fine_trace.note: Source. The remaining testcase bytes are materialized into the pull-parser context as the HTML document that later drives start-tag parsing and the crashing attribute scan.
Because the document begins with `<meta`, this predicate admits the sample as an HTML element and routes execution into start-tag parsing.

While parsing the initial `<meta charset=TSCII>` tag from the attacker-controlled document, the parser recognizes the `charset` attribute and forwards its attacker-controlled value to the encoding-switch logic.
For the attacker-supplied encoding name `TSCII`, the parser installs a non-UTF-8 decoder for subsequent bytes from the same document.
Later on the same parse, an unquoted attribute value is delegated to `htmlParseHTMLAttribute(ctxt, 0)`, placing the attacker-controlled attribute text on the vulnerable scanning path.

This loop scans the current attribute value until a terminator is seen. Reaching it depends on the earlier attribute-parsing call and on the continued parser state established from the attacker-controlled document.

Sink and root cause. The saved AddressSanitizer report shows that re-evaluating `CUR` at this loop header reads one byte past a one-byte global string object while parsing the attacker-controlled attribute text.

evidence_limitations: The saved sanitizer artifacts prove the sink in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` and the runtime call stack into attribute parsing, but they do not record the exact intermediate cursor/buffer state that made `CUR` point out of bounds at the crashing re-read.

The staged patch addresses memory-error propagation in converted-input growth, but Stage 02 does not treat that OOM path as a closed fact for this crashing run because the saved traces here do not directly observe it.

The testcase bytes prove the initial `<meta charset=TSCII>` prefix and the harness layout, but they do not by themselves identify the precise later attribute spelling at the crashing site; the GT therefore keeps the PoC contract at the exact reproduced witness rather than generalizing beyond the observed document.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is relevant to parser state around converted-input growth, but this Stage 02 trace does not claim dynamic fixed-build confirmation or a runtime-proven OOM sequence for the crashing run.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:symbolize=1 ./fuzz/html /gt/poc`, producing `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` with a size-1 READ in `htmlParseHTMLAttribute` at `HTMLparser.c:2759`.

format.name: OSS-Fuzz html testcase buffer
format.contract: The verified trigger contract is only the exact staged 256-byte witness. In the OSS-Fuzz HTML harness, the first 8 bytes are consumed as harness metadata (`opts` and `maxAlloc`) and the remaining 248 bytes are parsed as the HTML document, which for this witness begins with `<meta charset=TSCII>`. Source-grounded facts established here are limited to that exact document entering the parser, the parser admitting the initial `<meta` tag, switching decoding based on the attacker-controlled `charset=TSCII` attribute, later reaching `htmlParseHTMLAttribute(ctxt, 0)` for another attribute value, and crashing on the saved one-byte out-of-bounds `CUR` read at line 2759.
